nodes.label: v0.2 benchmark run with subagents and closed (#39), kg query fixes (#49), v0.2 report, examples for five projects (#53), benchmark v2 steps 1-2 (#52: hybrid, node cards)
nodes.description:
Goal: continue the project from the v0.2 benchmark (#39): run it, fix what it finds, write the decision report and plan v0.3.
Instructions: no Anthropic API key, run the benchmark with subagents; commit, push and open PRs only after the user's OK; scrapy is the large repo; rebuild and render graphs for five projects (basic-python-cli, my_first_data_project, python-clean-architecture, kg, scrapy) and update README, images and paths; open a separate issue for large-graph images if it applies.
Discoveries: on repos of 4-104 files the graph is as accurate as reading code but not cheaper; kg query had two checkability gaps (impact drowned in tests, untested without criterion); topic stores add nothing; a stale graph is safe but cannot answer what changed; the graph repeats README claims contradicted by workflow files; 96% of a graph-guided agent's context is kg's own output; with --brief cards the graph beats code (1.00, 63% less context); agent layers can cite stale lines; static PNGs of large graphs show false isolated nodes because hidden types take their edges.
Accomplished: bench.subagent runner; pilot (6) and 17 multi-hop questions with kg as fourth repo; #49 via PR #50 (impact --type, query tested, criterion); topic and stale variants; docs/benchmark.md report, PR #51 closes #39; issue #52 (benchmark v2, prio v0.3); #53 via PR #54 (five example graphs, scrapy agent layer, refreshed kg layer); issue #55 (large-graph overview); PR #56 (context metric, hybrid strategy); PR #57 (--brief node cards, function signatures, module line ranges, cards strategy, pinned kg agent layer for bench). All merged.
Next steps: let hybrid/cards read files kg status reports as changed or added; rest of #52 step 2 (Section nodes, quoted claims, workflow trigger extraction); #52 step 3 on scrapy (15-20 questions, code vs cards vs hybrid); #55; user to confirm version tags (v0.1.0 retroactive at 8b9d7b2, v0.2.0 after demo #40); #40 demo still open.
Relevant files: bench/subagent.py, bench/tools.py, bench/topics.py, bench/questions/main.json, bench/questions/stale.json, bench/agent/kg-1a342c4.json, bench/results/, docs/benchmark.md, src/kg/analysis.py, src/kg/cli.py, src/kg/extract/python.py, docs/query.md, examples/agent/scrapy.json, examples/agent/kg.json, docs/examples/

nodes.label: Run the benchmark with coding-agent subagents (bench.subagent), never with an API key
nodes.description:
What: bench.subagent has prepare (one prompt.md per question and strategy, no reference answer), call (the subagent's only tool: runs the confined strategy tool, logs to calls.jsonl, caps at 25 calls, stores the answer) and collect (grades with grading.py into result lines bench.report reads); each subagent gets a short bootstrap that cats its prompt.md.
Why: the user refused to use an Anthropic key; subagents need no credentials or spend approval.
Where: bench/subagent.py, bench/report.py, bench/README.md
Learned: only total subagent tokens are known (input/output columns empty) and ~28k of them are Claude Code's fixed prompt, so tokens hide strategy differences; at most 20 concurrent subagents; a run that exhausts its calls counts as max_turns, not retried; subagents work inside this repo and load AGENTS.md, a possible contamination on kg questions.

nodes.label: Benchmark pilot (6) and 17 multi-hop questions: code 0.94, graph 0.92; pilot too easy
nodes.description:
What: pilot 6 questions x code/graph all scored 1.00; 17 new multi-hop questions (kg pinned at 1a342c4 as fourth repo, references from an ast import graph independent of kg) gave code 0.94, graph 0.92 (16/17), graph slower with more calls.
Why: test whether the graph helps an agent (RNF-10); the pilot did not separate strategies, so harder questions with traps were added.
Where: bench/questions/main.json, bench/results/20261015T092017Z-subagent.jsonl, bench/results/20261015T093425Z-subagent.jsonl
Learned: graph failed pca-untested (walked tests one by one, ran out of 25 calls) and mfdp-auto-workflows (repeated README 'only flake8 is automatic' while CodeQL runs weekly by cron); the code 0.00 on pca-presenter-impl is a grader false negative (modules without src. prefix), so code is really 1.00; graph saves calls on transitive impact (2-4 vs 5-9); 5 graph runs truncated long JSON with head/python.

nodes.label: kg impact --type filters results (walk unchanged, omitted counts); kg query tested complements untested; both state the criterion
nodes.description:
What: kg impact --type T1,T2 lists only those types but still walks through others and reports omitted counts by type; kg query tested lists each element with the tests that point to it, sharing analysis.coverage with untested so both partition the same set; criterion (a test module imports it or a test function refers to it) in text and JSON 'criterion'; new JSON keys additive only.
Why: benchmark showed impact of kg.schema.validation gave 125 results, 109 Test nodes (57 KB JSON for 9 modules), and untested could not be trusted without its criterion.
Where: src/kg/analysis.py, src/kg/cli.py, docs/query.md, src/kg/agents/guide.md, .github/smoke-test.sh
Learned: --type Module cuts that impact to 3.6 KB; filtering Module alone misses Package nodes such as kg.extract (reported in omitted but the agent ignored it), so the guide recommends --type Module,Package.

nodes.label: Issue #49: answers an agent can check in one call (merged via PR #50)
nodes.description:
What: kg impact --type, kg query tested and the explicit tested criterion, with docs, guide, skill and smoke test.
Why: two benchmark failures of the graph strategy.
Where: PR #50, branch feat/49-query-checkable
Learned: re-running the graph strategy on the 17 questions: 0.92 -> 0.98, 17/17 answered, 7.5 -> 6.1 calls; pca-untested 0.00 (27 calls) -> 1.00 (6 calls) just from reading the criterion; one run per question, and the bench tool description changed too, so part may be noise.

nodes.label: kg impact with no --depth follows imports transitively and returns very broad results
nodes.description:
What: on kg itself a change reaches 100+ elements, mostly Test nodes.
Why: impact follows imports transitively by default; correct but noisy.
Where: src/kg/analysis.py
Learned: the benchmark showed the noise was tests, not depth; addressed by kg impact --type (#49) and --brief caps, default depth left unchanged.

nodes.label: Topic stores add nothing (0.98, -2% tokens); stale graph 0.63, always warns, never invents
nodes.description:
What: topic strategy (store with the question topic's types plus Repo/File/Config) on the 17 questions scored 0.98 like the full graph, 2% fewer tokens, more calls and time; kg-stale (graph of ebd078d over code of 1a342c4, 6 questions: 4 changed, 2 controls) scored 0.63 vs code 1.00: controls 1.00, changed answers 0.88-0.89 or 0.00.
Why: the roadmap's two benchmark variants (topic views, stale graph).
Where: bench/topics.py, bench/questions/stale.json, bench/repos.json (graph_commit), bench/results/20261015T095721Z-subagent-topic.jsonl, bench/results/20261015T095733Z-subagent-stale.jsonl
Learned: with impact --type, filtering at build time adds almost nothing, so RF-44 topic views move down; every stale answer mentioned the stale_graph warning and the 0.00s refused instead of inventing; staleness raises the priority of automatic refresh (RF-73/RF-78).

nodes.label: v0.2 verdict: graph as accurate as code but not cheaper on small repos; v0.3 starts with a large-repo benchmark, then freshness and doc-vs-code checks
nodes.description:
What: docs/benchmark.md answers the roadmap exit questions: code 1.00 (corrected), graph 0.98, same tokens, more time; graph saves calls on multi-hop, cites node IDs/edges, is safe when stale, but repeats docs that contradict code; topic views and calls relations move down; v0.3 starts with a large repo benchmark, then keeping the graph fresh and checking documents against code; if the graph does not win on the large repo, v0.3 starts the redesign the roadmap describes.
Why: v0.2 is the evidence phase (RNF-10); the hypothesis 'the graph helps an agent more than reading code' is not shown on small repos where reading code is cheap; the user agreed a larger repo is needed.
Where: docs/benchmark.md, docs/roadmap.md, README.md
Learned: limits stated in the report: 29 questions, one run each, small repos, possible AGENTS.md contamination; imports alone were enough for impact (calls relations not the bottleneck).

nodes.label: Issue #39: reproducible benchmark, code vs. knowledge graph (merged via PR #51)
nodes.description:
What: harness with code, graph and topic strategies, API and subagent runners, 6 pilot + 17 main + 6 stale questions, five result files and the docs/benchmark.md report.
Why: the main v0.2 item: evidence of whether kg helps an agent.
Where: bench/, docs/benchmark.md, PR #51
Learned: run entirely with subagents, no API key; PR #51 merged feat/49 so #50 had to merge first.

nodes.label: Issue #52 (first v0.3 item): benchmark v2, graph-guided reading, node cards and scrapy
nodes.description:
What: step 1 context metric + hybrid strategy (done, PR #56); step 2 node cards (done, PR #57) plus Section nodes for documents, quoted claims with source:lines and extraction of config facts such as workflow triggers (pending); step 3 scrapy with 15-20 checked questions, code vs graph/cards vs hybrid (pending); update docs/benchmark.md.
Why: v0.2 never tested graph-guided reading nor a repo too large to read; the user wants descriptive nodes that orient the agent so it loads only needed context and saves tokens.
Where: bench/, src/kg/, docs/benchmark.md; milestone v0.3, label prio:v0.3 (created this session)
Learned: proposed next order: let hybrid read files kg status reports as changed/added, then sections/claims, then scrapy; PRs use Refs #52, not Closes.

nodes.label: scrapy 2.19.0 (8026dee, BSD-3-Clause) is the large repo for the benchmark and examples
nodes.description:
What: scrapy pinned at release 2.19.0, commit 8026dee: 489 Python files (179 package, 302 tests), 76 .rst docs; kg extract gives ~7,900 nodes / 18,000 edges in 11 s.
Why: the user chose it; it is large enough (~300 modules with docs and tests) that reading the code is costly, where the graph should win; sphinx was the other candidate.
Where: issue #52, samples/README.md, docs/examples/licenses/scrapy.txt
Learned: BSD-3 (not MIT) so the license text is published alongside the example, relaxing the MIT-only rule for examples.

nodes.label: Issue #53: rebuild the example graphs for five projects, scrapy included (merged via PR #54)
nodes.description:
What: HTML and PNG for basic-python-cli (10/12), my_first_data_project (66/98), python-clean-architecture (398/754), kg at e18f574 (904/1889, refreshed 58-node agent layer) and scrapy (7964/18239, new 102-node agent layer written by a subagent with 4 documentation issues); README, docs/examples/README.md, examples/agent/README.md, samples/README.md updated; scrapy added to the published-layer test.
Why: published graphs predated kg query, consistent extraction and mandatory descriptions; kg and scrapy are the benchmark repos.
Where: docs/examples/, examples/agent/scrapy.json, examples/agent/kg.json, tests/test_flow.py
Learned: images of larger graphs show packages, modules and the agent layer (kg without classes, which formed a loose ring); edge counts first written in two README rows were invented and had to be corrected to real values (42, 35); the scrapy PNG is only a rough overview, its 8 MB HTML is the usable view.

nodes.label: Issue #55: overview of large graphs: lift edges of hidden nodes, separate components, thin the centre
nodes.description:
What: draw edges of hidden nodes to their nearest visible container (method->class->module->package), dashed and merged with counts; lay out components separately and pack them; drop or weaken contains/defines in the forces, try Kamada-Kawai under a size limit or an aggregated package view; keep determinism.
Why: in scrapy's image 61 of 435 visible nodes look isolated (16 of 97 in kg's), all with neighbours of a hidden type; 362 nodes and 1522 edges form one dense blob.
Where: src/kg/render/, docs/render.md
Learned: distinct from #35 (HTML layout time); static image first, then the HTML initial view.

nodes.label: Measure context chars per answer and add a hybrid strategy that reads only the ranges the graph cites
nodes.description:
What: every tool call logs chars of its result and each run reports context_chars (old logs replayed since tools are deterministic over pinned repo and store); hybrid = kg tool + read_file limited to files and line ranges in the provenance of nodes returned in that run (Citations, from provenance, not node IDs).
Why: subagent token totals are dominated by the fixed ~28k prompt; v0.2's graph strategy could not read files, which is not how kg is meant to be used.
Where: bench/subagent.py, bench/tools.py, bench/agent.py, bench/report.py (Context column)
Learned: the citation rule hides files kg status reports as added after the graph was built.

nodes.label: Hybrid scores 1.00 but loads more context than code: 96% is kg's own output
nodes.description:
What: hybrid on pilot, main and stale (29 runs): main 1.00 with mean/median context 14,888/9,758 chars vs code 11,974/7,385 and graph 14,640/11,998.
Why: step 1 of #52.
Where: bench/results/20261015T154218Z-subagent-hybrid-pilot.jsonl, ...154220Z-subagent-hybrid.jsonl, ...154222Z-subagent-hybrid-stale.jsonl, docs/benchmark.md
Learned: reading cited lines is 4% of context (~500 chars per read); kg output is 96% (query node 36%, find 27%, impact 24%); JSON is ~3x the text for the same node, mostly provenance repeated on every edge; hybrid fixed mfdp-auto-workflows by reading the cited workflow YAML and recovered one stale question.

nodes.label: --brief node cards on query node/find/path and impact, plus function signatures and module line ranges
nodes.description:
What: --brief gives a card per node (type, label, description, attrs, provenance once: method, source, lines, confidence below 1), one line per edge with provenance only when not the parser's, max 30 items with the rest counted by type (more; total for find); full answer stays the default; extractor adds attrs.signature to functions and test functions (shows fixtures) and provenance.lines [1, last] to modules and packages.
Why: 96% of a graph-guided agent's context was kg output; a card should give just enough to decide whether to open a file and which lines.
Where: src/kg/cli.py, src/kg/extract/python.py, docs/query.md, docs/extract.md, src/kg/agents/guide.md (tells agents to use --brief)
Learned: cuts answers 32% (path) to 85% (find); implemented as an output variant without touching query logic.

nodes.label: Cards (hybrid + --brief): 1.00 with 63% less context than code, first win for the graph; stale still 0.50
nodes.description:
What: cards strategy on 17 main + 6 stale: main 1.00, context 4,411/4,819 chars (mean/median) vs code 11,974, 31,395 tokens vs 34,637, 35 s vs 30 s; stale 0.50.
Why: step 2 of #52, measure the effect of the answer format alone.
Where: bench/results/20261015T160303Z-subagent-cards.jsonl, bench/results/20261015T160309Z-subagent-cards-stale.jsonl, docs/benchmark.md
Learned: ~3,200 fewer tokens per answer (about half without the 28k fixed prompt); less context on 12 of 17, gains largest on multi-hop, loses on lookups one search answers; stores were rebuilt with signatures so the gain mixes format and richer cards; one run per question; stale weak because the agent cannot open files added after the graph.

nodes.label: The benchmark pins kg's agent layer to its commit (bench/agent/kg-1a342c4.json)
nodes.description:
What: bench/repos.json uses bench/agent/kg-1a342c4.json, the layer as it was at 1a342c4, instead of examples/agent/kg.json.
Why: #53 refreshed examples/agent/kg.json for current code, so a fresh prepare against kg pinned at 1a342c4 failed.
Where: bench/agent/kg-1a342c4.json, bench/agent/README.md, bench/repos.json
Learned: every kg run in bench/results/ was built with that layer; benchmark inputs must not follow files that evolve with the code.

nodes.label: The agent layer repeats documentation that the code contradicts (mfdp README vs workflow triggers)
nodes.description:
What: in my_first_data_project the graph says only flake8 runs automatically (from the README) while CodeQL also runs weekly by cron; graph strategy scored 0.67.
Why: agent layers inherit doc errors and kg extract does not read workflow triggers.
Where: examples/agent layers, src/kg/extract (config)
Learned: hybrid fixes it by reading cited workflow files; #52 step 2 plans quoted claims with source:lines and extraction of config facts so contradictions can be flagged (CU-03).

nodes.label: Agent-layer nodes can cite stale line ranges
nodes.description:
What: the decision node used by kg-decision-html cited docs/requirements.md:279, which at 1a342c4 is the heading '## 9. Out of scope'.
Why: agent layers are written once and lines move as docs change; nothing checks them.
Where: bench/agent/kg-1a342c4.json, examples/agent/*.json
Learned: only visible once the agent can read what is cited (hybrid); evidence for quoted claims and Section nodes in #52 step 2.

nodes.label: Let hybrid/cards read files that kg status reports as changed or added
nodes.description:
What: extend the read_file citation rule to files kg status marks as changed or added since the graph was built.
Why: the stale graph is the remaining weak spot (cards 0.50); the agent sees kg status naming new files but cannot open them.
Where: bench/tools.py, bench/subagent.py
Learned: proposed as the next, small step before scrapy; hybrid already recovered a stale question by reading a cited file that had changed.

nodes.label: Grader scores 0 a correct answer that omits the src. module prefix
nodes.description:
What: pca-presenter-impl.code was correct but wrote modules without the src. prefix and got 0.00, so code's 0.94 is 1.00 corrected.
Why: name normalization in the grader does not strip src-layout prefixes.
Where: bench/grading.py
Learned: reports quote both the raw and corrected code score instead of changing published results.

nodes.label: Version tags per milestone: v0.1.0 retroactive at 8b9d7b2, v0.2.0 after the demo (#40)
nodes.description:
What: proposal: tag v0.1.0 on 8b9d7b2 now, and v0.2.0 when #40 closes, with a PR that bumps __version__.
Why: the user asked whether to tag each milestone.
Where: git tags, src/kg __version__
Learned: tags and releases are public, so waiting for the user's confirmation (asked twice, no answer yet).
